plain: The story is that in 2023 Congress came close to passing a law that would protect people holding UFO secrets so they could speak, and that a few lawmakers gutted it. The UFO campaigner Steven Greer says on the show that the bill was meant to give them 'safe harbor or amnesty', and that it was cut down by Turner, Rogers, Pelosi and others. The tellers link it to the UAP Disclosure Act, a Senate amendment to the yearly defense bill put forward on 13 July 2023 (UAP being the government's current term for UFOs). Dan Sheehan, a lawyer who says he took part in the push, names Mike Turner as the main obstacle. He stresses that Turner is the Ohio congressman whose district includes Wright-Patterson, an Air Force base, and he mentions Representative Dan Crenshaw. Michels says in his own voice that 'the last time around the UAPDA was killed by Mike Turner.' If true, a handful of members of Congress blocked a route to disclosure. Greer and Michels give it as their own account, and Sheehan as someone involved.
